samples.summary: Attacker-controllable GitHub issue bodies are interpolated verbatim into the new verifier/explorer prompts, and the verifier's output is now the sole source of both the confirm verdict and the citations the gate checks
samples.evidence: `loadContext` (hunt-ui.mjs:717 region) builds `context.issues` from `fetchIssues` → `renderIssues`, which slices each issue `body` to 600 chars and concatenates it with no fence/delimiter escaping (scripts/agent/hunt-corpus.mjs:135-136). That string is dropped inside a triple-backtick block in the explorer prompt (hunt-ui.mjs:270-272) and in the verifier prompt (hunt-ui.mjs:404-407). Anyone who can file an issue on the public repo (`--state all`, so closed issues count too) can put ``` plus instructions in the body and escape the fence. The prompt labels the block "DATA", which is mitigation by request only. What makes this materially worse in this PR than in hunt.mjs: the UI explorer has no `citations` field, so `uiCitationsOf` sources the gate's stage-4 citations from the verifiers' own `groundedIn` (hunt-ui.mjs uiCitationsOf, consumed at hunt-gate.mjs:542). A single influenced verifier stream therefore supplies BOTH the `confirmed`/`high`/ground decision and the `file:line` evidence that is supposed to be independent of it — and nothing checks that the cited file exists, only `CITATION.test` + `citationInScope` (hunt-gate.mjs:428-433,546-551). Blast radius is bounded (report only, no filing; explorer/verifier hold only Read/Grep/Glob plus the bounded browser tool, and the report is redacted), so the realistic impact is a maintainer-facing false report steered by an outsider rather than code execution or credential theft.

samples.summary: Two new run artifacts (`hunt-ui-execution.json`, `repro-N.json`) are written with no `redactSecrets` pass while every sibling artifact gets one
samples.evidence: `report.md` (hunt-ui.mjs:848-861), `run.json` (:854-859) and `explore-raw.json` (:955-965) all go through `redactSecrets` with `extra: [context.cfg.apiKey]`. `writeFileSync(path.join(outDir, "hunt-ui-execution.json"), JSON.stringify(sessionLog))` at :863 does not, and neither does the repro plan write at :1099 (`JSON.stringify({ actions: cand.actions })`). `sessionLog` holds raw SDK result messages (ask.mjs:523 pushes the message unmodified), i.e. model-authored text; `cand.actions` holds model-authored `type` text from a session whose agent has Read/Grep/Glob over the repo, so a value read out of a local `.env`-style file and typed into the browser would land in a plan file unredacted — the same plan a maintainer is told to paste/replay from a report. `.harness-reports/` is gitignored (.gitignore:173), which bounds exposure to the local machine, and hunt.mjs:1132 has the same unredacted execution-log write, so this is a continued pattern rather than a new one. Searched: all `redactSecrets`/`writeFileSync`/`writeArtifact` call sites in scripts/agent/hunt-ui.mjs and hunt.mjs, plus `redactSecrets` in hunt-probe.mjs:41.
searchedFor: read hunt.mjs:1109-1140 for the equivalent CLI writes

samples.summary: A deliberate input-corrupting fault injector now lives in application source, gated only by a build-time `import.meta.env.DEV` constant with no runtime guard
samples.evidence: `installFault` (page.tsx:112-128) attaches a capture-phase keydown listener that `preventDefault()`s every second printable keystroke, switched on purely by the `?fault=` query string (page.tsx:85-92, wired at :239). I verified the claimed gate: App.tsx:42-44 wraps the lazy import in `import.meta.env.DEV ? … : null` and App.tsx:89-91 renders the route conditionally, so the module is statically eliminated from a production build, and no other importer exists (grep `harness/hunt` finds only App.tsx, the runner and verify-hunt-oracles.mjs). Two reasons it is still worth flagging: (a) any dev-mode build served anywhere — a preview deploy, `vite dev` exposed beyond localhost, or a build with `--mode development` — exposes `/harness/hunt?fault=drop-second-char` unauthenticated (the route sits outside `PrivateRoute`), and (b) the three sibling harness routes (`/harness/visual`, `/harness/interaction`, `/harness/docs`, App.tsx:83-88) are NOT DEV-gated, so the single gate this file depends on is one consistency refactor away from disappearing, and the file's own comment argues against adding a second one. Impact is contained because the route mounts `MemStore`/`MemDocStore` with no backend, so corrupted keystrokes cannot reach real data.

samples.summary: `persona.id` is validated only as a non-empty string yet is used to build read and write filesystem paths, so a manifest id containing `../` escapes the report directory
samples.evidence: `validatePersona` checks `typeof p.id !== "string" || p.id === ""` (hunt-ui.mjs:122) and nothing about its shape. That id is then interpolated into paths in two directions: `loadPersonas` reads `path.join(dir, `${p.id}.md`)` (:~105 in the diff hunk), and `runHunt` writes into `path.join(outDir, persona.id)` (:927) — `explore-raw.json` and `repro-N.json` (:1099). An id such as `../../../../tmp/x` therefore reads an arbitrary `.md` and writes attacker-chosen JSON outside `.harness-reports`, and `--charters-dir` lets the manifest come from any directory. The trust boundary is repo config (personas.json is committed), so exploitation needs a merged change or a hostile `--charters-dir`, which is why this is hardening rather than an open hole; `validateCharter` in hunt.mjs:116-136 has the identical gap, so a fix should cover both. Searched: validatePersona/validateCharter bodies, every use of `persona.id`/`c.id` in path construction in hunt-ui.mjs and hunt.mjs.
searchedFor: grep persona.id and personaDir in hunt-ui.mjs

samples.summary: The gate's permitted-grounds allow-lists are exported as mutable `Set`s, so any importing module can widen the gate at runtime
samples.evidence: `UI_GROUNDS = new Set(UI_VERIFIER_SCHEMA.properties.confirmationGround.enum)` and `SHARED_GROUNDS = new Set([...])` are exported unfrozen, and `UI_GATE_OPTIONS = Object.freeze({ grounds: UI_GROUNDS, … })` (hunt-ui.mjs) freezes only the wrapper, not the Set. `isFilingVerdict` stage 3 asks `grounds.has(v.confirmationGround)` (hunt-gate.mjs:526), so a single `UI_GROUNDS.add("looks-wrong")` anywhere in the process admits the exact ground the schema test at hunt-gate.test.mjs deliberately forbids — and that test inspects the schema, not the Set, so it would not notice. All callers are first-party, so this is defence-in-depth only; `Object.freeze` on the Set (or exposing a frozen array plus a lookup function) closes it.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding is present as described. renderIssues (hunt-corpus.mjs:131-140) slices attacker-supplied issue bodies to 600 chars and concatenates them with no escaping of backticks or fence delimiters; fetchIssues (hunt-corpus.mjs:142-153) pulls --state all, so any outsider who can file (or comment on a body of) an issue on the public repo contributes text. loadContext (hunt-ui.mjs:709) puts that string in context.issues, and it is interpolated verbatim inside triple-backtick blocks in both the explorer prompt (hunt-ui.mjs:270-273) and the verifier prompt (hunt-ui.mjs:404-407). The only mitigation is the prose label "NOT findings (DATA)" — instruction-level, not structural; note the sibling replayEvidence block IS passed through redactSecrets (hunt-ui.mjs:401) while context.issues is not, confirming no sanitizer covers this path. The escalation specific to this hunter is real: uiCitationsOf is literally verdicts.flatMap(v => v.groundedIn) (hunt-ui.mjs:185-187), wired in as UI_GATE_OPTIONS.citationsOf (hunt-ui.mjs:190) and consumed at hunt-gate.mjs:542, and the verifier prompt states "You are the ONLY source of the code location" (hunt-ui.mjs:384-387). So a single prompt-influenced verifier stream supplies BOTH the stage-3 confirmed/high/ground decision (hunt-gate.mjs:515-531) and the stage-4 citations, which are checked only by CITATION.test (hunt-gate.mjs:546-548) and citationInScope's glob-to-regex path match (hunt-gate.mjs:428-433) — nothing verifies the cited file or line exists. I considered already-guarded via stage 1's trusted deterministic replay (hunt-gate.mjs:485-489), but it does not close the vector: a steered explorer can produce a candidate whose bogus expectation fails deterministically, which passes replay, after which the influenced panel supplies the confirmation and in-scope citations. Tool grants are read-only plus the bounded browser tool (hunt-ui.mjs:88-91,329,432), so blast radius is a maintainer-facing false report rather than code execution — which is exactly the bounded impact the reviewer claimed at major, not an inflated severity. Untrusted external input flowing unescaped into an LLM prompt whose output is the sole source of a gate decision falls squarely under this lens's injection / unsafe-input-handling lane, and major is blocking under this rubric.
